clue.text: Creature a soldier captures abroad

indicators.note: captures means the soldier holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
abroad means out, away from home

explanation.surface: A soldier serving overseas takes some animal prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a burrowing rodent of Central and South America, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Red or white wine, good at parties

parts.note: raves are wild parties

explanation.surface: A wine that goes down well at any party, whether red or white.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux wine region producing both red and white wines.

clue.text: Stressed no more than nineteen qualified at last

parts.note: nineteen or fewer is under a score, a score being twenty

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word qualified

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that no more than nineteen people finally qualified.
explanation.definitionFit: To underscore a point is to emphasise it, so underscored means stressed.

clue.text: Aware Keith somehow has inscribed name on top of the present

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on top of another comes before it
has inscribed means the jumbled name has another letter written into it
somehow says the letters of Keith are to be rearranged in some way

parts.note: the present moment is now

explanation.surface: Keith somehow manages to engrave a name on a gift he is handing over.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'somehow' gives ITHEK, and 'has inscribed' writes N into it after the I; 'present' looks like a gift but means now.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the know is an idiom for being informed, which is to say aware.

clue.text: Bring to a conclusion nevertheless, proceeding very quickly

parts.note: but can mean nevertheless or however
ton-up is British slang for going at a hundred miles an hour, especially on a motorbike

explanation.surface: Someone wraps things up regardless, while rushing along.
explanation.walkthrough: TON-UP is British slang for travelling at 100 mph, a ton being a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To button up a deal or job is an idiom for completing it or bringing it to a conclusion.

clue.text: Spell inhaling pot leads to physical collapse

indicators.note: inhaling means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a spell of activity is a bout
an urn is a kind of pot or vase

explanation.surface: A session of smoking cannabis brings on bodily breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' wants to be cannabis, with 'inhaling' as smoking; it is simply an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnout is exhaustion and collapse brought on by overwork or stress.

clue.text: Cloth to flog after cutting

indicators.note: after cutting means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to welt is to beat or flog, raising weals

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric is used to whip someone once it has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cutting' docks the last letter of the flogging word, leaving WEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a piece of absorbent cloth for drying.

clue.text: Orthodox leader, one limiting black magic

indicators.note: limiting means the two letters enclose another between them
leader means the first letter of the word Orthodox

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An Orthodox church leader keeps the dark arts in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, or obeah, is a kind of sorcery or witchcraft practised in the Caribbean.

clue.text: City dweller thrown out by a tribune

indicators.note: thrown out signals the letters being scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman tribune expels someone who lives in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An urbanite is a person who lives in a town or city.

clue.text: One authorises girlfriend briefly to enter house

indicators.note: to enter means a piece goes inside the house

parts.note: a manor is a large country house

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a date is someone one goes out with, here a girlfriend

explanation.surface: Someone gives permission for his girlfriend to come into the house for a short visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandator is one who issues a mandate, that is, one who authorises or commands.

clue.text: A little bit close to northern resort

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in not a whit
by means near or close to

explanation.surface: A seaside town in the north lies a short distance away.
explanation.walkthrough: WHITBY is a seaside resort on the coast of North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitby is a coastal holiday town in northern England.

clue.text: Academic qualification obtained from inside Greece

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diploma earned while studying in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A university degree is a standard academic qualification.

clue.text: Paints with colour ———- that'll give an edge

parts.note: oils are oil paints
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Paints and colour that lend a picture its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilstone is a whetstone, oiled and used for sharpening blades.

clue.text: I was put in with the rest into the exam, not the practical

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: into means a piece is placed inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

indicators.note: was put in means the letter goes inside the next piece

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest

explanation.surface: A candidate grumbles about being sent into the written exam with everyone else rather than the practical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was put in' makes ETIC; 'into' then sets that inside the exam word to give ORETICAL. 'the practical' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition's contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretical work is concerned with theory rather than practice, the opposite of practical.

clue.text: Labour schedules about a day to go in pursuit of Tory voters

indicators.note: to go in pursuit of means this piece follows after the other

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: about means the stints surround the day

parts.note: stints are allotted periods of work
Tue is short for Tuesday

explanation.surface: Labour plans a day of campaigning to chase after Conservative supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' and 'Tory' look like UK parties; Labour here is work, and only Tory is the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Constituents are the electors who make up a constituency, the voters an MP represents.

clue.text: Designer also introduced by film director on set out east

indicators.note: introduced by means the piece is brought inside the director's name

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director
too means also

indicators.note: out means the following letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A designer is brought in by the director on the film set out east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from SET to leave ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist designs and inks pictures onto skin, so is a kind of designer.

clue.text: Stormy Weather has a hold on a singer

indicators.note: has a hold on means the jumbled word grips another letter inside it
stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of Weather are churned up

explanation.surface: The song Stormy Weather has a firm grip on a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'Stormy' turns the weather word into WHEATER, which then grips the A. 'Stormy Weather' looks like the song title, and 'singer' a vocalist; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird, and crosswords often call a bird a singer.

clue.text: Dress — terribly swish attire, right?

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters being badly disordered

explanation.surface: A dress that is awfully swish clothing, isn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'right?' looks like a tag question; it supplies R to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirtwaister is a dress with a bodice styled like a shirt.

clue.text: Trouble one large town almost completely banned

parts.note: ill means trouble or harm
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: almost completely means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Trouble in a big town where nearly everything is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illicit is forbidden by law, banned.

clue.text: Understood, getting to the end of a French translation

indicators.note: getting to the end of means this piece comes after the other

parts.note: un is French for a
seen means understood, as in I see

explanation.surface: A student grasps the point at the end of a French translation.
explanation.walkthrough: An UNSEEN is a passage set for translation without preparation, a staple of British school exams.
explanation.definitionFit: An unseen is a piece of translation done at sight, without prior study.

clue.text: Henry and William given notice

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written
Bill is a short form of William

explanation.surface: Two men named Henry and William are served notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbill is a printed notice distributed by hand.

clue.text: Preserved, like former Peruvian empire

definitions.meaning: kept in a tin, read as two words
relating to the Inca people, whose empire ruled Peru

explanation.definitionFit: Inca describes the ancient Andean empire, and split into two words it describes food kept in a tin.

clue.text: Planning itinerary right away for excursion

indicators.note: away means the letter is taken out

parts.note: routing is planning the route or itinerary

explanation.surface: Organising the route for a day trip without a right turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short trip or excursion.

clue.text: Broken lances in old battle site

indicators.note: broken signals the letters smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Snapped lances lie on an ancient battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: SENLAC is the name given to the hill where the Battle of Hastings was fought in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Senlac Hill is the traditional site of the Battle of Hastings.

clue.text: Gigot is part of course

definitions.meaning: gigot is a ... of mutton or lamb
a stage of a race or journey

explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a cut of meat from the limb, and a stage of a course is also called by that name.

clue.text: Class makes gradual progress, and finally settles

parts.note: cl is the abbreviation for class
inches means moves forward bit by bit

explanation.surface: A class slowly moves forward and eventually comes to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal or argument is to settle it conclusively.

clue.text: Rats consuming dead fish

indicators.note: consuming means the first piece swallows the second

parts.note: rats and drat are both mild exclamations of annoyance
gone means dead

explanation.surface: Rodents eat a dead fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' looks like animals; it is the exclamation, DRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragonet is a small, often brightly coloured sea fish.

clue.text: Gift of story book

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT, the New Testament, counts as a book

explanation.surface: A present of a storybook.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude.
